data.description:
## Context / Problem
`rebar claim` (via `claim_gate_check` in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py`, which calls
`signing.verify_signature` -> `verify_opcert_record` in `src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:517-535`)
unconditionally rejects a plan-review op-cert whose `principal` differs from the local
environment's `own_principal`, returning `verdict: "foreign_key"` and refusing to claim.

Reproduced 2026-08-28: `review_plan` run through the rebar MCP server (principal
`9f1c8e42-...`) signed and returned `"signature":{"signed":true}` (a genuine PASS). The
subsequent `rebar claim <id>` from this checkout's local CLI/venv (a different environment,
principal `b8a354e0-...`) failed with:
```
no certified plan-review attestation (signature: foreign_key; op-cert signed by a different
environment (principal '9f1c8e42-...'; this environment is 'b8a354e0-...'))
```
Re-running `review-plan` locally (same environment as the later `claim`) succeeded, confirming
the attestation itself was valid — only the environment mismatch blocked the claim.

## Why this is a bug, not intended behavior
`docs/releasing.md` / AGENTS.md / ADR 0104 decision 3 state that op-cert environment-binding is
**advisory, not enforced**, until an operator explicitly sets `verify.require_environment` +
`verify.opcert_enforce_since` together (`infra/runbooks/mcp-opcert-enforcement-flip.md`). This
project's `rebar.toml` sets neither. The standalone `rebar verify-opcert` command (
`src/rebar/_commands/verify_opcert.py`) correctly honors this: "`verify.require_environment`
unset -> advisory everywhere (exit 0)". But the CLAIM-gate path (`verify_opcert_record` in
`_opcert_signing.py`, reached via `claim_gate_check`) has NO such config check — it hard-rejects
any cross-environment `principal` unconditionally, regardless of
`require_environment`/`opcert_enforce_since`. So a project that has NOT opted into environment
enforcement still cannot claim a ticket whose plan-review was legitimately signed by a different
environment (e.g. the MCP server vs. a local CLI worktree) — the "advisory" promise is broken in
practice for this one gate.

## Impact
Any agent whose plan-review runs through the rebar MCP server (a different signing environment
than its local `rebar` CLI/worktree) cannot claim the ticket it just got PASSED review on, without
either re-running the review locally (wasteful, doubles LLM cost) or a human using `--force`
(policy-disallowed for agents). This directly blocked cutting the rebar 0.13.0 release ticket.

## Reproduction
1. Have two environments configured with different `REBAR_OPCERT_ENV_ID` (e.g. the MCP server
   container vs. a local checkout), neither `verify.require_environment` nor
   `verify.opcert_enforce_since` set in `rebar.toml`.
2. Run `review-plan <ticket>` via environment A (e.g. rebar-mcp) -> PASS, signed.
3. Run `rebar claim <ticket>` from environment B (local CLI).
4. Observe `foreign_key` denial, even though environment enforcement is not configured.

## Suggested fix
`claim_gate_check` / `verify_opcert_record`'s claim-path check should consult
`verify.require_environment` + `verify.opcert_enforce_since` (mirroring `verify_opcert.py`'s
logic) before treating a cross-environment `principal` as disqualifying. When enforcement is not
configured, a structurally-valid signed attestation from ANY environment should satisfy the claim
gate (still validating the DSSE/sshsig signature itself when the verifying environment has the
matching public key; when it does not, the enforcement-off path should not fail the claim solely
for that reason).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: With `verify.require_environment`/`opcert_enforce_since` unset, `rebar claim` accepts a certified plan-review attestation signed by a different registered environment (no `foreign_key` denial).
- [ ] AC2: With `verify.require_environment` + `opcert_enforce_since` both set (enforcement flipped on), `rebar claim` still rejects an attestation from an environment other than the required one, or one predating the enforcement pin.
- [ ] AC3: A regression test in `tests/unit/` covers both the advisory (AC1) and enforced (AC2) configurations for the claim-gate path specifically (not just `verify-opcert`).
- [ ] AC4: `docs/plan-review-gate.md` documents this cross-environment acceptance behavior and its interaction with the enforcement flip.

## Testing
- New/updated tests exercising `claim_gate_check` / `verify_opcert_record` under both configs.
- `make test` passes.
data.title: Claim gate hard-rejects cross-environment plan-review op-certs even when environment enforcement is not configured
